subject: Planets in the morning sky, November 2026
query: is there a planet alignment in november 2026
title: Is there a planet alignment in November 2026? What to see at dawn
answer: Yes, in the morning sky. Around Nov. 12, 2026, Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter line up before sunrise, and Mars passes about one degree from Jupiter on Nov. 14-17. Venus and Mercury sit low in the southeast, and Mercury is best around Nov. 20. The planets only look close together from Earth; they are not physically near each other.
body:
Popular Science says the four planets form a line before dawn around Nov. 12: Venus in the southeast, Mars high in the east, Jupiter lower in the east and Mercury low in the southeast just before sunrise. The three bigger planets stay roughly in line all month.

The highlight is the pairing of Mars and Jupiter. BBC Sky at Night Magazine says Mars passes around a degree north of Jupiter, with closest approach on Nov. 14-17. Jupiter, at about magnitude -2.0, will look far brighter than reddish Mars, at about +0.7. Popular Science lists Nov. 16 as the conjunction date, with the bright star Regulus nearby. No telescope is needed, but do not point binoculars toward the horizon once the sun is up.

Mercury reaches its greatest western elongation, its best morning position, on Nov. 20, with brilliant Venus just above it. The Leonid meteor shower is predicted to peak on Nov. 18, usually at 10 to 15 meteors an hour, and the Full Beaver Moon on Nov. 24 is the first of three supermoons in a row.
in_the_news: Four planets line up in the predawn sky in mid-November 2026, with a close Mars-Jupiter conjunction on Nov. 14-17.

faq.q: What planets are lined up in the morning sky in November 2026?
faq.a: Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter, visible before sunrise.

faq.q: When are Mars and Jupiter closest in November 2026?
faq.a: Nov. 14-17, when Mars passes about one degree north of Jupiter in the predawn sky.

faq.q: Is there a planet parade tonight?
faq.a: Not in the evening. This month's lineup is a morning event; look east and southeast in the hour before sunrise.

faq.q: What is the bright star in the east before sunrise?
faq.a: In November 2026 it is most likely Venus, the brightest planet, low in the southeast, or Jupiter higher in the east.

faq.q: When is the best day to see Mercury in November 2026?
faq.a: Around Nov. 20, its greatest western elongation, low in the southeast before sunrise.

faq.q: Do I need a telescope to see the planet alignment?
faq.a: No. Venus, Jupiter and Mars are bright enough to see with the naked eye. Mercury is harder to spot because it stays low near the horizon.
